The Float64 Datatype columns have number values with decimals. The Int64 Datatype columns have number values with whole numbers (integers). The object Datatype columns have a variety of datatypes, these could be string/text values (e.g., ‘Mobile Homes’ for in.geometry_building_type_recs), binned/discrete data (e.g., ‘0-20%’ bin for in.area_median_income), or numbers with accompanying units (e.g., ‘25 ACH’ for in.infiltration). 9 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications. Task 2: Local open-source data comparison In a review of the local open-source building stock data provided by PBC representatives, there was alignment between several building stock data points from local building stock data and the ResStock data. These include the number of residential building units, the total population, the number of occupants in different sized homes (i.e., number of units), a comparison of income to renter/owner status, a comparison of building type and number of units, and a comparison of renter, owner, and vacant unit counts. This was unsurprising given the fact that this local data was primarily based on results from the American Community Survey, which is also one of the national surveys leveraged by ResStock. However, there were some valuable data points provided by PBC that focused on cost burdened households and households of color, neither of which are reported on by ResStock. While these data points did not inform the remainder of the work, they were included in Appendix B given their importance to programmatic decisions. Task 3: Modeled energy consumption, utility bill, and emissions impact for low-income households with upgrades Energy consumption impacts Along with information about the PBC building stock, ResStock also has data about the modeled energy consumption of this baseline building stock and the modeled change in energy consumption as a result of 16 different upgrades packages. Based on one of our early meetings with representatives from PBC, the focus of our remaining analysis will be on low-income households as defined as households at 150% or less of the Federal Poverty Line. The upgrade packages are different combinations of the individual upgrades found in Table 1. Additionally, the right-hand column in Table 1 shows those packages that were analyzed for PBC. A full list of the upgrade package combinations can be found in Table C-1 in Appendix C.
